title: Wait on a periodic flush and shutdown with tokio::select!
summary: Select over an interval and a oneshot, then replace the cancel-unsafe read_line with next_line on Lines.

turns.user: this only flushes after 100 lines so at night stuff sits there for minutes. flush every 5s too. also ill send shutdown over a oneshot when stopping, flush whats left and exit when it comes

assistant.body: Here's the plan: tokio::select! waits on the next line, a tick and shutdown at the same time. Note: a sleep created inside the loop is rebuilt every time a line arrives, so it never fires while lines keep coming within 5 seconds. The interval is created once outside the loop and the loop awaits tick on it. Its first tick completes immediately, so flush now does nothing on an empty batch. MissedTickBehavior::Delay stops ticks from firing in a burst after a slow flush.

turns.user: works but sometimes lines show up downstream with the start cut off. seems to line up with the tick

assistant.body: I need to correct myself. read_line is not cancel safe. When the tick completes first, select! drops the half-finished read_line future. The bytes it already took out of the BufReader are lost there, and the next read_line starts in the middle of a line. Moving line out of the loop does not help, because its contents after a cancel are not guaranteed.

next_line on the Lines returned by lines() is cancel safe. A partial line stays inside Lines and comes back complete on the next call. next_line also strips the trailing newline, which matters if downstream expects it.

turns.user: fixed. also they say 5s floods downstream, make it 30

assistant.body: Understood. Only the interval period changes. The flush at 100 lines stays, so behavior during busy hours is the same.
